body: @orangeshyguy21 this would probably also take a migration step that cleans up seeds across keyset entries if an encrypted seed is present.

Differential-fuzzing note on `cashu/core/p2bk.py` (legacy NUT-28 helper, not in this diff, so a conversation comment): `derive_blinding_scalar` masks the slot with `slot_index & 0xFF`, so slot 256 silently derives slot 0's key — reproduced against the published v3 slot-0 vector. The legacy reference snippet in 28.md does the same, but the v3 normative text requires the opposite ("Both sides MUST enforce the cap: a 256th leaf key would wrap onto slot 0's tweak... refused rather than truncated"). One-line guard fixes it. Also flagged on cashubtc/nuts#443 so the reference snippet stops contradicting the rule.
@ye0man agreed, it's blocked on LND upstream exposing allow_self_payment on those RPCs.

Reviewed. The fix is sound and minimal.

`_proof_from_row()` correctly maps the lowercase `c` column to `Proof.C`, overriding the key pydantic was silently dropping. Checked against the schema and the DB layer:

- `c` exists in both `proofs_used` and `proofs_pending` (see migrations.py).
- `fetchall()` returns SQLAlchemy `RowMapping` objects (`cashu/core/db.py`), so `dict(row)` / `row["c"]` work the same way across SQLite, Postgres, and CockroachDB — this isn't SQLite-specific.
- `Proof.C` has no alias, so the leftover lowercase `c` key in the merged dict is harmless (pydantic ignores unknown fields by default) — no collision with the explicit `"C"` override.
- `Proof.Y` is recomputed from `secret` in `__init__` regardless of row contents, confirming double-spend protection (keyed by `Y`) was never affected, as the issue states.

All three call sites that are actually wired into `Ledger` are covered (`get_pending_proofs_for_quote`, `get_proofs_pending`, `get_proofs_used` in `cashu/mint/crud.py`) — confirmed by checking every caller of these methods across the repo.

Tests look well-targeted: one does an end-to-end melt and checks both the raw `c` column and `get_proofs_used`, the other round-trips a pending proof. They reuse existing helpers/conventions from this file. I didn't have a Python 3.10–3.12 interpreter available to actually run them, so I can't confirm "fail on main, pass here" myself — just noting that as unverified on my end, not as a doubt about the PR.

One gap, not introduced by this PR and not currently live: `cashu/mint/auth/crud.py` has the identical `Proof(**r)` pattern in three places (`get_pending_proofs_for_quote`, `get_proofs_pending`, `get_proofs_used`, lines ~317/332/686) for the blind-auth proof tables. Same latent bug. I checked — none of those three auth-crud methods are called anywhere in the repo today, so it's dead code rather than a live issue, but it's the same landmine sitting in a parallel file and would be a natural follow-up (either in this PR or separately).

No blocking correctness issues found. Approve modulo the above.
Hello, thanks for your work. However, we already have idempotency of the endpoints with Redis caching of successful responses. I think this is not needed.

> @orangeshyguy21 this would probably also take a migration step that cleans up seeds across keyset entries if an encrypted seed is present.

I explored coverage this would provide, and came to the same conclusion. A simple migration is probably worth it here.
I added `m040`, which clears `seed` wherever `encrypted_seed` is set. 

`m018` rebuilds rows through `MintKeyset`, which now keeps the ciphertext. So a 0.15.0–0.15.2 mint with encryption on that upgrades straight to this release gets duplicate rows with both seed and ciphertext. `encrypt.py migrate` skips those as "already migrated".

Rows the bug leaked as plaintext-only (`encrypted_seed` NULL) are left alone, since encrypting them needs `MINT_SEED_DECRYPTION_KEY`. Currently handled. by the manual `encrypt.py migrate`.

The same `Proof(**r)` pattern is still in `cashu/mint/auth/crud.py`: `get_pending_proofs_for_quote` (L317), `get_proofs_pending` (L332) and `get_proofs_used` (L686). The auth tables also store the signature as `c` (`auth/migrations.py` L71/L89), so those getters still return proofs with an empty `C`. Might be worth using `_proof_from_row` there too, e.g. by moving it somewhere both crud modules can import.

`exclude_none=True` drops more than `pubkey`. `expiry` is `None` whenever `mint_quote_ttl` is unset and the invoice has no expiry tag (`ledger.py` L651-655), and `updated_at` is `None` for quotes stored before that column was added (it was added `DEFAULT NULL` with no backfill; `from_row` keeps the `None`). On this branch:

```python
q = MintQuote(..., expiry=None, updated_at=None, pubkey=None)
sorted(PostMintQuoteResponse.from_mint_quote(q).model_dump(exclude_none=True))
# [amount, amount_issued, amount_paid, method, quote, request, state, unit]
```

So `expiry` and `updated_at` vanish from those responses too, not only `pubkey`. Maybe exclude just `pubkey` when it is unset.
Is this only an LND issue?

Thanks @orangeshyguy21.

Tested ACK e062b167 for the encrypted-storage and m040 cleanup changes, including keyset rotation and reloading the same derived keys.

I also reproduced a pre-existing issue with the plaintext-only recovery command recommended in the PR description.

With SQLite, Python 3.13.7, and SQLAlchemy 2.0.37, running `python -m cashu.mint.encrypt migrate --no-dry-run` against a disposable database containing a plaintext-only keyset fails after confirming the update:

```text
Updating keysets in the database.
sqlalchemy.exc.ArgumentError: List argument must consist only of tuples or dictionaries
```

Encryption and the decryption self-check succeed in memory, but the ciphertext is not persisted.

The UPDATE in `cashu/mint/encrypt.py` passes a flat tuple with `?` placeholders through the connection wrapper to `AsyncSession.execute(text(query), values)`. This execution path needs named bind parameters and a dictionary, following the existing CRUD convention:

```python
await conn.execute(
    f"UPDATE {ledger.db.table_with_schema('keysets')} "
    "SET seed='', encrypted_seed = :cipher, "
    "seed_encryption_method = :method WHERE id = :id",
    {
        "cipher": keyset_dict["encrypted_seed"],
        "method": keyset_dict["seed_encryption_method"],
        "id": keyset_dict["id"],
    },
)
```

This is not introduced by this PR, but it affects the recommended recovery procedure because m040 intentionally leaves plaintext-only rows untouched.

Could we include the binding fix and a CLI regression test here, or address them in a linked follow-up PR?
